R24.3: Böckle's presentation, his Lemma 2 (finite plus no more relations than variables gives a finite flat complete intersection) and Theorem 1, KW Annals Theorem 3.3, the lift types of KW I Theorem 5.1 (definition with API and tests) and its four constructions from KW II §10.3.1, the application table, and Snowden's prescribed-type lifts for the modern route. R24.5:operations: compatible systems with separate strict/almost strict/plain predicates, and twist, restriction, induction. R24.6: residual members, what almost strictness gives at the coefficient prime, and linked systems. Finiteness (R24.1) and points (R24.2) belong to part R23.1. Math. 154 (2003) 179–198), not in Khare's paper with Böckle's appendix [26] (found while carrying the draft EXT-12 in part R23.1). nodes.title: Böckle's presentation of a global deformation ring (Proposition 1 of the appendix)
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(k) be odd and absolutely irreducible, X a set of local deformation conditions, unramified outside a finite set S, and d ∈ {0, 1}, Ad_X = Ad⁰ρ̄ if X fixes the determinant (d = 0) and Ad_X = Adρ̄ otherwise (d = 1). Suppose (a) for ℓ ∈ S ∖ {p, ∞} the local ring R_{X,ℓ} is a complete intersection, flat over ℤ_p, of relative dimension h⁰(G_ℓ, Ad_X) − Δ_ℓ, and (b) R_{X,p} is a complete intersection, flat over ℤ_p, of relative dimension h⁰(G_p, Ad_X) + 1 + d − Δ_p. Then with Δ = ΣΔ_ℓ, R_X ≅ 𝒪⟦x₁, …, x_{n+d}⟧/(f₁, …, f_{n+Δ}) for some n. In particular, when Δ ≤ 0 (for instance minimal conditions, where Δ_ℓ = 0) the ring has at most as many relations as variables (Böckle's Corollary 1; KW Annals Proposition 3.4: W⟦X₁, …, X_r⟧/(f₁, …, f_s) with r ≥ s).

Böckle [1], Theorem 5.6: R_X ≅ 𝒪⟦x₁, …, x_{n+d}⟧/J with J generated by at most Σ j_ℓ elements.
Count n + d from the tangent space with the global Euler characteristic (oddness) to get n + Δ = Σ j_ℓ.

nodes.title: Finite plus few relations gives a finite flat complete intersection (Böckle's Lemma 2)
nodes.statement: Let 𝒪 be a discrete valuation ring and R a complete noetherian local 𝒪-algebra, finitely generated as an 𝒪-module, with a presentation R ≅ 𝒪⟦x₁, …, x_n⟧/(f₁, …, f_m) with m ≤ n. Then m = n, (π, f₁, …, f_n) is a regular sequence, and R is a complete intersection, finite and flat over 𝒪; in particular R[1/π] ≠ 0, so R has a point over the integers of a finite extension of Frac 𝒪.
hypotheses: finiteness over 𝒪 is essential: 𝒪⟦x⟧/(0) has m = 0 ≤ n = 1 but is not finite, and is not a complete intersection of dimension 1 over 𝒪 in the required sense
this is the commutative-algebra core of "finiteness plus presentation gives lifts"; KW II use the same principle in the form of their Corollary 4.7 (R24.2)

In a regular local ring a system of parameters is a regular sequence, so (π, f₁, …, f_n) is regular: R is a complete intersection and π is a nonzerodivisor on R, i.e. R is flat over 𝒪.

nodes.title: Minimally ramified lifts (Khare–Wintenberger, Annals, Theorem 3.3)
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) be of S-type with p > 2, ρ̄|_{ℚ(µ_p)} absolutely irreducible, 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 and k(ρ̄) ≠ p. Then ρ̄ has a lift that is minimally ramified at every prime; when k(ρ̄) = p + 1 it may be chosen of crystalline type (Hodge–Tate weights (0, p)) or of semistable type (weight 2). Proof: the minimal deformation ring R^univ has a presentation with r ≥ s (Böckle, Proposition 3.4), is finite over W (Proposition 3.8: Lemma 3.6 reduces finiteness to finiteness of the universal mod-p image, which follows from Taylor's potential modularity and Fujiwara's R = T over a totally real F), hence is finite flat and a complete intersection (Theorem 3.7), so it has a point in characteristic zero. This is the method suggested in the Remark in §5.2 of Khare–Ramakrishna, Finiteness of Selmer groups and deformation rings (Invent. Math. 154 (2003) 179–198, KW Annals' [27]; not Khare's paper with Böckle's appendix, which is [26]), which the later KW II Theorem 5.1 generalises.

nodes.title: Lifts of required type (KW I Theorem 5.1 (1)–(4))
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) be of S-type with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 if p > 2, non-solvable image if p = 2, and ρ̄|_{ℚ(µ_p)} absolutely irreducible if p > 2. A lift ρ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝒪′) of ρ̄ is of required type (i) if: (1) (k(ρ̄) = 2 when p = 2) ρ is minimally ramified at every ℓ ≠ p and crystalline of weight k(ρ̄) at p; (2) ρ has weight 2, is minimally ramified at ℓ ≠ p, and its inertial Weil–Deligne parameter at p is (ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0), or (id, N) with N ≠ 0 nilpotent when k(ρ̄) = p + 1 (k(ρ̄) = 4 if p = 2); (3) for an odd q ∥ N(ρ̄) with p | q − 1, ρ̄|_{I_q} = (χ ∗; 0 1): ρ is as in (2) at p and minimal at ℓ ≠ p, q, and ρ|_{I_q} ≅ (χ′ ∗; 0 1) for a character χ′ = ω_q^i (0 < i ≤ q − 2) lifting χ, with i even if p = 2; (4) for q ≠ p with ρ̄|_{D_q} ≅ (χ_p ∗; 0 1) up to unramified twist and p | q + 1: ρ is as in (2) at p and minimal at ℓ ≠ p, q, and ρ|_{I_q} ≅ χ′ ⊕ χ′^q for a level-2 character χ′ = ω_{q,2}^iω_{q,2}^{qj} of p-power order, with i + j even if p = 2. nodes.title: Compatible systems: strict, almost strict, and plain
nodes.statement: For a number field E and number field F, an E-rational two-dimensional strictly compatible system (ρ_ι) of G_F consists of: for each prime ℓ and embedding ι : E ↪ ℚ̄_ℓ, a continuous semisimple geometric ρ_ι : G_F → GL₂(ℚ̄_ℓ); for each prime 𝔮 of F a Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation r_𝔮 with values in GL₂(E), unramified for almost all 𝔮, such that for every ℓ and ι the Weil–Deligne parameter of ρ_ι|_{D_𝔮} is conjugate to r_𝔮 (for 𝔮 above ℓ too, via Fontaine); and integers a ≥ b with Hodge–Tate weights (a, b). nodes.title: Rank-n weakly compatible systems of l-adic representations
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field. A rank n weakly compatible system of l-adic representations ℛ of G_F defined over M is a 5-tuple (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_λ}, {H_τ}): M a number field; S a finite set of primes of F; for each prime v ∉ S a monic degree-n Q_v(X) ∈ M[X]; for each prime λ of M (residue characteristic l) a continuous semisimple r_λ : G_F → GL_n(M̄_λ) such that for v ∉ S with v ∤ l, r_λ is unramified at v and r_λ(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial Q_v(X), and for v | l, r_λ|_{G_{F_v}} is de Rham, and crystalline if v ∉ S; and for each τ : F ↪ M̄ a multiset H_τ of n integers with HT_τ(r_λ) = H_τ for every M̄ ↪ M̄_λ over M. Rank 1 systems are weakly compatible systems of characters. Over ℚ this is Taylor's 'rank d weakly compatible system' with Hodge numbers {n_1, …, n_d} (Documenta 2006, p. 773), who asks only for crystallinity at l ∉ S and Hodge–Tate numbers at every λ. The rank-2 systems of R24.5/compatible-system (Khare–Wintenberger, Dieulefait–Pacetti) carry Weil–Deligne data r_𝔮 at every prime and are compared with these through R24.5/compatible-system-predicates ('strictly compatible').
hypotheses: RS-12: this node is the common carrier; it contains representations at the coefficient places, not only common traces, and the weak, almost-strict and strict conditions stay separate predicates
M-rationality of Frobenius polynomials and independence of the Hodge–Tate multisets are part of the data, not theorems
proofSteps: Definition; the only verification is that each condition is stable under the choice of M̄ ↪ M̄_λ (conjugation).
A newform of weight k ≥ 2 gives a rank-2 system with S the primes dividing the level (Deligne; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1).

nodes.title: Linear-algebra operations on weakly compatible systems and what they preserve
nodes.statement: Direct sums, tensor products, duals, symmetric and exterior powers, restriction and induction of weakly compatible systems are weakly compatible, by applying the operation to each r_λ: for example ℛ^∨ = (M, S, {X^nQ_v(0)^{−1}Q_v(X^{−1})}, {r_λ^∨}, {−H_τ}); for F′/F finite, ℛ|_{G_{F′}} has S^{(F′)} the primes above S, H^{(F′)}_τ = H_{τ|_F} and Q^{(F′)}_v with roots α^{[k(v):k(v|_F)]} for α the roots of Q_{v|_F}. Preservation: strict compatibility and (strict) purity are preserved by all of these (weights add under ⊗, change sign under duality, scale under Sym^k and ∧^k); regularity is preserved by duality and restriction but not in general by ⊗, Sym^k or induction (Hodge–Tate multisets can collide); irreducibility is preserved by duality but not by restriction; automorphy is preserved by duality and restriction to solvable extensions, and by the other operations only under the corresponding functoriality (not assumed).

nodes.title: Residual irreducibility over F(ζ_l) for a density-one set of primes
nodes.statement: Let ℛ be a regular weakly compatible system of l-adic representations of G_F defined over M (BLGGT Proposition 5.2.2). For a subrepresentation s of r_λ write s̄ for the semisimplification of its reduction and l for the rational prime below λ. There is a set L of rational primes of Dirichlet density 1 such that if s is an irreducible subrepresentation of r_λ with λ above an element of L, then s̄|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} is irreducible.
hypotheses: ℛ = (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_λ}, {H_τ}) a weakly compatible system of l-adic representations of G_F of rank n (R24.5/weakly-compatible-system-rank-n); ı : M ↪ ℂ.
ℛ regular.
proofSteps: Take F¹ from BLGGT Lemma 5.2.1 (R24.5/rank-two-reducibility-independent-of-lambda). Regularity gives an element of G_λ⁰ with n distinct eigenvalues (Harris–Taylor VII.1.8, I.2.2); Frobenius elements at primes split in F¹ are Zariski dense in G_λ⁰; after enlarging M (Galois over ℚ) every r_λ is integral and the irreducible constituents of r_λ|_H, H open, are defined over M_λ with multiplicity one.

For r_l = ε_l ⊕ ⊕_{λ|l} r_λ: the Zariski closure G_l with open image Γ_l (Bogomolov), F⁰ independent of l, the connected centre Z_l, C_l = G_l⁰/G_l^der, the simply connected cover G_l^{SC} with central kernels of order dividing a uniform A, and Serre's θ_l : S_l → C_l, whose exponents m_{μ,σ} are bounded by a constant B independent of l.

Larsen's density-one set L: l unramified in M and F⁰ with ℛ unramified above l (so r_l crystalline), l ≥ 4B + 4, G_l⁰ unramified, a semisimple model G̃_l^{SC}/ℤ_l with G̃_l^{SC}(ℤ_l) the preimage of the image of G_{F⁰} and perfect, and standard reductions of the constituents.
Two constituents agreeing on G̃_l^{SC}(ℤ_l) × Γ_l^{Z,1} differ by a power ε_l^b: solve Σ_i (m_{1,Frob^i σ_v} − m_{2,Frob^i σ_v})l^i = b(l^{f_v} − 1)/(l − 1) digit by digit using the bound B.

Write s ≅ Ind_{Γ_l¹}^{Γ_l} s₀ with s₀ an irreducible Γ_l⁰-constituent; since l is unramified in F⁰, s̄|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} ≅ Ind s̄₀ over ker ε_l, irreducible because a conjugate s̄₀^γ ≅ s̄₀ε_l^a forces a = 0 (γ has finite order).
acceptance: Check the case n = 1: every s̄ is a character, so the conclusion holds with L the set of all primes.

Check that the conclusion is the residual hypothesis of BLGGT Theorem 5.4.1 (4), ¯r|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} irreducible, for every irreducible constituent s and not only for r_λ, and that it is asserted only on a density-one set of l: this is the precise condition under which irreducibility passes to reductions that R24.5:operations records.
Check the dependencies: Larsen 1995 (1.12–1.13, 2.6, 3.15, 3.17) and Larsen–Pink 6.14 are recorded as gaps, not proved here.

nodes.title: Constituents of an essentially conjugate self-dual system
nodes.statement: Let F be CM or totally real, ℛ a pure, extremely regular weakly compatible system over M, and ℳ a character system of G_{F⁺} with (ℛ, ℳ) essentially conjugate self-dual. For a finite extension F′/F and a subrepresentation s of r_λ|G_{F′}, there is a CM field F″ with F ⊆ F″ ⊆ F′ such that s is invariant by G_{F″}; (s, μ_λ) is essentially conjugate self-dual, and totally odd if (r_λ, μ_λ) is (Lemma 5.2.3).
hypotheses: F CM or totally real; ℛ pure and extremely regular; (ℛ, ℳ) essentially conjugate self-dual.
proofSteps: Choose τ so that distinct equal-size subsets of H_τ have distinct sums (extreme regularity) and τ₁ on the normal closure F₁ of F′/F⁺; submodules of the same dimension are equal iff the Hodge–Tate numbers of their determinants agree, so constituents have multiplicity one.
Purity gives h_σ + h_{σc} = w dim s, so s^{σcc′} = s^σ; the group generated by products cc′ of complex conjugations cuts out the maximal CM subfield F″ of F′, and s extends to G_{F″}.
Comparing Hodge–Tate numbers, s^c ≅ μ_λ s^∨, realised by restricting the pairing matrix A_{λ,v}; this gives the parity statement.
acceptance: Check that extreme regularity, not only regularity, is what is used: it separates equal-dimensional submodules by the Hodge–Tate numbers of their determinants, which gives multiplicity one of the constituents of r_λ|_{G_{F₁}}.

Check the output against R24.5/linear-algebra-operations-on-systems: restriction to G_{F′} may break irreducibility, and the lemma records what survives for polarized systems (each constituent descends to a CM field F″ ⊆ F′ and stays essentially conjugate self-dual with the same μ_λ, totally odd if (r_λ, μ_λ) is).

The definitions of S-type, k(ρ̄), N(ρ̄) and "modular" used in KW I Theorems 4.1 and 5.1.
Langlands' solvable base change and descent for Hilbert modular forms, as used in KW II §§9–10 (descent of modularity along allowable base changes; the π_i of the Brauer argument).
Weil–Deligne parameters of ℓ-adic representations and their compatibility with twist, restriction and induction.
Artin conductors and their behaviour under reduction.
Residual images: absolute irreducibility and oddness of residual members.
Recognition of semisimple representations by Frobenius polynomials (Brauer–Nesbitt with Chebotarev).

The local L-factor L(WD, s) and the local constant ε(WD, ψ, s) of a Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation of W_{F_v}, F_v/ℚ_p finite, with Deligne's normalisation: additivity, inductivity in degree zero, and the unramified case ε = 1 when WD and ψ are unramified. BLGGT §5.1 take ψ_v(x) = ψ_p(tr_{F_v/ℚ_p}(x)) with ψ_p|_{ℤ_p} = 1 and ψ_p(1/p) = e^{−2πi/p}, and form ε(ıℛ, s) as the product of ε(ıWD_v(ℛ), ψ_v, s) over finite v with the archimedean and Hodge factors.

Brauer's induction theorem for a finite group G over ℂ: 1 = Σ n_i Ind_{H_i}^G ψ_i in the virtual character ring with n_i ∈ ℤ, H_i elementary (hence soluble) and ψ_i linear characters, together with the induced-character formula, Frobenius reciprocity and Mackey's formula of Layers 2–3. BLGGT §5.4 (8)(f) apply it to G = Gal(F′/F) and transport it to ℓ-adic Galois representations by ı^{−1}.
